129	# --- figure data: (data, checks) ----------------------------------------------------------
130	
131	def m1_returns(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
132	    """M1: 2x against 1x window returns. A breached 2x path has no 2x return, so it is left out."""
133	    both = paired.dropna(subset=["return_1x", "return_2x"])
134	    checks = {}
135	    for t in tickers_in(paired["ticker"]):
136	        w = both[both["ticker"] == t]
137	        checks[t] = {"windows_with_both_returns": int(len(w)),
138	                     "above_twice_1x": int((w["return_2x"] > 2 * w["return_1x"]).sum()),
139	                     "breached_2x": int((paired.loc[paired["ticker"] == t, "breached_2x"] == True).sum())}  # noqa: E712
140	    return both, checks
141	
142	
143	def m2_gap(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
144	    """M2: the exact log gap against its approximation −Σr² (expectation 1), windows without a breach."""
145	    ok = paired.dropna(subset=["exact_gap", "approx_gap"])
146	    checks = {"windows_without_breach": int(len(ok)),
147	              "largest_exact_gap": float(ok["exact_gap"].max()),
148	              "largest_identity_difference": float((ok["log_gap"] - ok["exact_gap"]).abs().max()),
149	              "median_relative_error": {t: float(ok.loc[ok["ticker"] == t, "approx_rel_error"].median())
150	                                        for t in tickers_in(ok["ticker"])}}
151	    return ok, checks
152	
153	
154	def m3_drawdown(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
155	    """M3: 2x against 1x maximum drawdown with the bound 1 − (1 − MDD_1x)² (expectation 2)."""
156	    ok = paired.dropna(subset=["mdd_1x", "mdd_2x", "mdd_bound"])
157	    below = ok["mdd_2x"] < ok["mdd_bound"] - BOUND_TOL
158	    checks = {t: {"windows": int((ok["ticker"] == t).sum()), "below_bound": int(below[ok["ticker"] == t].sum())}
159	              for t in tickers_in(ok["ticker"])}
160	    return ok, checks
161	
162	
163	def m4_turnover(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
164	    """M4: the 2x path's mean daily turnover per window (expectation 4); breached windows have none."""
165	    ok = paired.dropna(subset=["mean_turnover_2x"])
166	    checks = {t: {"windows": int((ok["ticker"] == t).sum()),
167	                  "median_mean_turnover_2x": float(ok.loc[ok["ticker"] == t, "mean_turnover_2x"].median())}
168	              for t in tickers_in(ok["ticker"])}
169	    return ok, checks
170	
171	
172	def m5_breaches(paired: pd.DataFrame, run: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
173	    """M5: the 2x NAV of every window whose 2x path was breached (expectation 3), from path_days."""
174	    breached = paired[paired["breached_2x"] == True]  # noqa: E712
175	    paths = []
176	    for t in tickers_in(breached["ticker"]):
177	        days = read_table(run / "path_days", columns=[*KEY, "leverage", "day", "date", "daily_return", "nav"],
178	                          filters=[("ticker", "=", t)])
179	        paths.append(days[days["leverage"] == 2.0].merge(breached.loc[breached["ticker"] == t, KEY], on=KEY))
180	    data = (pd.concat(paths, ignore_index=True) if paths
181	            else pd.DataFrame(columns=[*KEY, "leverage", "day", "date", "daily_return", "nav"]))
182	    breach_returns = sorted({float(r) for r in data.merge(
183	        breached[[*KEY, "breach_date_2x"]], on=KEY).query("date == breach_date_2x")["daily_return"]})
184	    checks = {"breached_windows": int(len(breached)), "tickers": tickers_in(breached["ticker"]),
185	              "breach_dates": sorted({str(d) for d in breached["breach_date_2x"]}),
186	              "breach_day_returns": breach_returns,
187	              "all_use_an_unverified_day": bool(breached["contains_unverified_day"].all())}
188	    return data, checks
189	
190	
191	def s1_sensitivity(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
192	    """S1: exact medians of the 1x and 2x returns over all windows and over the windows without an
193	    unverified day, as analysis/sql_sensitivity.py computes them for 2x (percentile 0.5, nulls left out)."""
194	    rows = []
195	    for t in tickers_in(paired["ticker"]):
196	        w = paired[paired["ticker"] == t]
197	        plain = w[w["contains_unverified_day"] == False]  # noqa: E712
198	        for leverage, column in (("1x", "return_1x"), ("2x", "return_2x")):
199	            rows.append({"ticker": t, "leverage": leverage,
200	                         "all_windows": int(w[column].count()), "all_median": float(w[column].median()),
201	                         "unflagged_windows": int(plain[column].count()),
202	                         "unflagged_median": float(plain[column].median()) if plain[column].count() else math.nan})
203	    data = pd.DataFrame(rows)
204	    checks = {f"{r.ticker} {r.leverage}": {"all_windows": r.all_windows, "all_median": r.all_median,
205	                                           "unflagged_windows": r.unflagged_windows,
206	                                           "unflagged_median": r.unflagged_median} for r in data.itertuples()}
207	    return data, checks
208	
209	
210	def d1_returns(snapshot: Path) -> tuple[tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame], dict]:
211	    """D1: every daily return of the snapshot, with the unverified extreme days of its quality report."""
212	    returns = pd.concat([read_table(f, columns=["ticker", "date", "daily_return"])
213	                         for f in sorted((snapshot / "daily_returns").glob("*.parquet"))], ignore_index=True)
214	    returns = returns.dropna(subset=["daily_return"])
215	    report = json.loads((snapshot / "quality_report.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
216	    flagged = pd.DataFrame([{"ticker": d["ticker"], "date": pd.Timestamp(d["date"]).date()}
217	                            for d in report.get("unverified_extreme_days", [])], columns=["ticker", "date"])
218	    flagged = flagged.merge(returns, on=["ticker", "date"], how="left")
219	    checks = {"unverified_extreme_days": int(len(flagged)),
220	              "unverified_days_without_a_return": int(flagged["daily_return"].isna().sum())}
221	    for t in tickers_in(returns["ticker"]):
222	        r = returns[returns["ticker"] == t]
223	        checks[t] = {"returns": int(len(r)), "first_date": str(r["date"].min()), "last_date": str(r["date"].max()),
224	                     "unverified_extreme_days": int((flagged["ticker"] == t).sum())}
225	    return (returns, flagged), checks
226	
227	
228	def d2_windows(windows: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
229	    """D2: the entry date of every window definition, and whether it uses an unverified day."""
230	    config = json.loads((windows / "config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
231	    defs = read_table(windows / config["windows_file"], columns=[*KEY, "contains_unverified_day"])
232	    checks = {t: {"windows": int((defs["ticker"] == t).sum()),
233	                  "use_an_unverified_day": int(defs.loc[defs["ticker"] == t, "contains_unverified_day"].sum())}
234	              for t in tickers_in(defs["ticker"])}
235	    return defs, checks
236	
237	
238	def measured_runs(csv: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
239	    """The runs an experiment's summaries use: not warm-ups, ended ok, and in a used protocol where the
240	    CSV marks one (the stride experiment's CSV does not)."""
241	    rows = pd.read_csv(csv)
242	    keep = (rows["warmup"] == False) & (rows["status"] == "ok")  # noqa: E712
243	    if "used" in rows:
244	        keep &= rows["used"] == True  # noqa: E712
245	    return rows[keep]
246	
247	
248	def summarize(rows: pd.DataFrame, by: str, metric: str) -> dict:
249	    """Per group, in order of first appearance: the runs, the experiment's own time metric (median and
250	    range), the phase medians, and peak total RSS in GiB (median and range)."""
251	    out = {}
252	    for key, g in rows.groupby(by, sort=False):
253	        peak = g["peak_rss_total_bytes"] / 2**30
254	        out[str(key)] = {"runs": int(len(g)), "metric": metric, "median_s": float(g[metric].median()),
255	                         "min_s": float(g[metric].min()), "max_s": float(g[metric].max()),
256	                         "phases_s": {p: float(g[f"{p}_s"].median()) if g[f"{p}_s"].notna().any() else math.nan
257	                                      for p in PHASES},              # pandas has no session start: undefined
258	                         "peak_median_gib": float(peak.median()), "peak_min_gib": float(peak.min()),
259	                         "peak_max_gib": float(peak.max())}
260	    return out
261	
262	
263	STRIDE_LABELS = {"baseline": "stride {}, first", "planned": "stride {}", "exploratory": "stride {}, exploratory",
264	                 "drift_check": "stride {}, repeated"}
265	
266	
267	def x1_stride(csv: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
268	    """X1: the stride experiment, per protocol in the order they ran; its time metric is wall_s (no plan
269	    capture). The repeated stride 21 is the drift check, and stride 3 is exploratory (experiments.md)."""
270	    rows = measured_runs(csv).sort_values(["protocol_id", "run_id"])
271	    rows = rows.assign(label=[STRIDE_LABELS[r.role].format(r.stride) for r in rows.itertuples()])
272	    protocols = summarize(rows, "label", "wall_s")
273	    for label, c in protocols.items():
274	        first = rows[rows["label"] == label].iloc[0]
275	        c.update({"protocol": str(first["protocol_id"]), "role": str(first["role"]), "stride": int(first["stride"]),
276	                  "windows": int(first["windows"])})
277	    baseline = next(c for c in protocols.values() if c["role"] == "baseline")
278	    repeated = next((c for c in protocols.values() if c["role"] == "drift_check"), None)
279	    drift = (repeated["median_s"] - baseline["median_s"]) / baseline["median_s"] if repeated else None
280	    return rows, {"protocols": protocols, "drift_of_the_repeated_protocol": drift}
281	
282	
283	def x2_partitions(csv: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
284	    """X2: the shuffle-partition experiment's configurations; time metric wall_excl_capture_s."""
285	    rows = measured_runs(csv)
286	    return rows, summarize(rows, "config", "wall_excl_capture_s")
287	
288	
289	def x3_baseline(csv: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
290	    """X3: the pandas baseline's implementations S and P; time metric wall_s (no plan capture)."""
291	    rows = measured_runs(csv)
292	    return rows, summarize(rows, "engine", "wall_s")
293	
294	
295	def x4_caching(csv: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
296	    """X4: the caching experiment's configurations; time metric wall_excl_capture_s."""
297	    rows = measured_runs(csv)
298	    return rows, summarize(rows, "config", "wall_excl_capture_s")
299	
300	
301	# --- drawing ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
302	
303	def _panels(n: int, row_height: float = 2.9):
304	    """One axes per ticker, three to a row; a spare axes, if any, holds the legend."""
305	    cols = min(n, 3)
306	    rows = math.ceil(n / cols)
307	    fig, grid = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=(3.6 * cols + 0.4, row_height * rows + 0.9), squeeze=False)
308	    axes = list(grid.ravel())
309	    for spare in axes[n:]:
310	        spare.axis("off")
311	    return fig, axes[:n], (axes[n] if len(axes) > n else None)
312	
313	
314	def _finish(fig, title: str, note: str | None = None, xlabel: str | None = None, ylabel: str | None = None,
315	            legend_from=None, legend_in=None, legend_on_top: bool = False) -> None:
316	    """Title, shared axis labels, legend and footnote, with room for each measured in inches. The legend
317	    goes into `legend_in` (a spare axes), into a band under the title (`legend_on_top`), or where it fits."""
318	    height = fig.get_figheight()
319	    note_room = 0.36 if note else 0.0              # up to two lines of 7-point text
320	    label_room = 0.32 if xlabel else 0.0
321	    top_room = 0.36 + (0.3 if legend_on_top else 0.0)
322	    fig.suptitle(title, x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
323	    if legend_from is not None:
324	        handles, labels = legend_from.get_legend_handles_labels()
325	        if legend_on_top:
326	            fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 1 - 0.4 / height),
327	                       ncol=len(labels), frameon=False)
328	        else:
329	            (legend_in or legend_from).legend(handles, labels, loc="center" if legend_in else "best", frameon=False)
330	    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0.03 if ylabel else 0, (note_room + label_room) / height, 1, 1 - top_room / height))
331	    if xlabel:
332	        fig.supxlabel(xlabel, y=(note_room + 0.05) / height, va="bottom", fontsize=8.5)
333	    if ylabel:
334	        fig.supylabel(ylabel, x=0.004, ha="left", fontsize=8.5)
335	    if note:
336	        fig.text(0.01, 0.06 / height, note, fontsize=7, color="0.35", ha="left", va="bottom", wrap=True)
337	
338	
339	def _percent(ax, x: bool = True, y: bool = True) -> None:
340	    if x:
341	        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1.0, decimals=0))
342	    if y:
343	        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1.0, decimals=0))
344	
345	
346	def _by_flag(ax, w: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str) -> None:
347	    for flag, color, label in ((False, PLAIN, "window without an unverified day"),
348	                               (True, FLAGGED, "window that uses an unverified day")):
349	        part = w[w["contains_unverified_day"] == flag]
350	        ax.scatter(part[x], part[y], s=5, color=color, alpha=0.55, linewidths=0, label=f"{label}")
351	
352	
353	def draw_m1(data: pd.DataFrame, checks: dict):
354	    tickers = list(checks)
355	    fig, axes, spare = _panels(len(tickers))
356	    for ax, t in zip(axes, tickers):
357	        w, c = data[data["ticker"] == t], checks[t]
358	        _by_flag(ax, w, "return_1x", "return_2x")
359	        xs = np.array([w["return_1x"].min(), w["return_1x"].max()]) if len(w) else np.array([0.0, 0.0])
360	        ax.plot(xs, 2 * xs, color=GUIDE, lw=0.9, ls="--", label="twice the 1x return")
361	        ax.set_title(f"{t}: 2x above the line in {c['above_twice_1x']} of {c['windows_with_both_returns']}")
362	        if c["breached_2x"]:
363	            ax.text(0.03, 0.97, f"{c['breached_2x']} windows with a breached 2x path not shown (M5)",
364	                    transform=ax.transAxes, va="top", fontsize=6.5, color="0.35")
365	        _percent(ax)
366	    _finish(fig, "M1  The 2x window return against twice the 1x return", note=overlap_note(),
367	            xlabel="1x window return", ylabel="2x window return", legend_from=axes[0], legend_in=spare)
368	    return fig
369	
370

542	def _draw_groups(checks: dict, labels: dict[str, str], title: str, metric: str, note: str):
543	    """Medians and ranges of the experiment's time metric and peak memory, and the phase medians, per group."""
544	    keys = list(checks)

549	                                   (ax_m, ("peak_median_gib", "peak_min_gib", "peak_max_gib"), "{:.2f} GiB")):
550	        mids, los, his = (np.array([checks[k][f] for k in keys]) for f in (mid, lo, hi))
551	        ax.bar(x, mids, yerr=[mids - los, his - mids], color=[colors[k] for k in keys], width=0.6, capsize=3,
552	               error_kw={"lw": 0.9})
553	        for xi, m, h in zip(x, mids, his):        # the median's label sits above the range, not on it
554	            ax.annotate(fmt.format(m), (xi, h), xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=7)

558	    ax_m.set_ylabel("peak total RSS (GiB): median and range")
559	    width = 0.8 / len(keys)

563	                 label=labels[k].replace("\n", " "))
564	    ax_p.set_xticks(np.arange(len(PHASES)), PHASE_LABELS)
565	    ax_p.set_ylabel("phase time (s): median")
566	    ax_p.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=7)
567	    _finish(fig, title, note=note)
568	    return fig

664	def compare_documented(results: dict) -> list[str]:
665	    """Every difference between the checked numbers and DOCUMENTED (for the default inputs only)."""
666	    doc, problems = DOCUMENTED, []
667	
668	    def same(label, got, want):
669	        if got != want:
670	            problems.append(f"{label}: {got}, documented {want}")
671	
672	    def pct(value):
673	        return None if value is None else round(100 * value, 1)
674	
675	    m1, m2, m3, m4, m5 = (results[k][1] for k in ("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5"))
676	    s1, d1, d2 = results["S1"][1], results["D1"][1], results["D2"][1]
677	    for t, n in doc["windows"].items():           # a ticker missing from the results is a difference, not an error
678	        d2t, m1t, m3t = d2.get(t, {}), m1.get(t, {}), m3.get(t, {})
679	        s1x, s2x = s1.get(f"{t} 1x", {}), s1.get(f"{t} 2x", {})
680	        same(f"D2 {t} windows", d2t.get("windows"), n)
681	        same(f"D2 {t} windows with an unverified day", d2t.get("use_an_unverified_day"),
682	             doc["windows_with_an_unverified_day"][t])
683	        same(f"M1 {t} above twice the 1x return", (m1t.get("above_twice_1x"), m1t.get("windows_with_both_returns")),
684	             doc["above_twice_1x"][t])
685	        same(f"M3 {t} windows below the bound", m3t.get("below_bound"), 0)
686	        same(f"S1 {t} median 1x return", pct(s1x.get("all_median")), doc["median_return_1x_percent"][t])
687	        same(f"S1 {t} median 2x return and windows", (pct(s2x.get("all_median")), s2x.get("all_windows")),
688	             doc["median_return_2x_percent"][t])
689	    tsla = s1.get("TSLA 2x", {})
690	    same("S1 TSLA 2x median and windows without an unverified day",
691	         (pct(tsla.get("unflagged_median")), tsla.get("unflagged_windows")), doc["tsla_2x_unflagged"])
692	    same("M2 windows without a breach", m2["windows_without_breach"], doc["windows_without_breach"])
693	    same("M2 largest exact gap is at most 0", m2["largest_exact_gap"] <= 0, True)
694	    errors = m2["median_relative_error"]
695	    same("M2 lowest and highest median relative error",
696	         ((round(100 * min(errors.values()), 1), min(errors, key=errors.get)),
697	          (round(100 * max(errors.values()), 1), max(errors, key=errors.get))), doc["median_relative_error_range"])
698	    turnover = {t: c["median_mean_turnover_2x"] for t, c in m4.items()}
699	    same("M4 lowest and highest median turnover",
700	         ((round(100 * min(turnover.values()), 1), min(turnover, key=turnover.get)),
701	          (round(100 * max(turnover.values()), 1), max(turnover, key=turnover.get))), doc["median_turnover_range"])
702	    same("M5 breaches", {"windows": m5["breached_windows"], "tickers": m5["tickers"], "dates": m5["breach_dates"],
703	                         "returns_percent": [round(100 * r, 1) for r in m5["breach_day_returns"]]}, doc["breaches"])
704	    same("M5 every breached window uses an unverified day", m5["all_use_an_unverified_day"], True)
705	    same("D1 unverified extreme days", d1["unverified_extreme_days"], doc["unverified_extreme_days"])
706	    same("D1 unverified days without a return", d1["unverified_days_without_a_return"], 0)
707	    groups = {"X1": results["X1"][1]["protocols"], **{k: results[k][1] for k in ("X2", "X3", "X4")}}
708	    for figure_id, documented in ((k, doc[k]) for k in ("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4")):
709	        for group, values in documented.items():
710	            c = groups[figure_id].get(group, {})
711	            same(f"{figure_id} {group} median time and peak",
712	                 (three_decimals(c.get("median_s")), three_decimals(c.get("peak_median_gib"))), values)
713	    drift = results["X1"][1]["drift_of_the_repeated_protocol"]
714	    same("X1 drift of the repeated stride 21", pct(drift), doc["X1_drift_percent"])
715	    return problems
716	
717	
718	def three_decimals(value):
719	    """A number rounded as the experiment documents report it: three decimals."""
720	    return None if value is None else round(value, 3)
721	
722	
723	def _rounded(value):
724	    if isinstance(value, float):
725	        return None if math.isnan(value) else round(value, 6)
726	    if isinstance(value, dict):
727	        return {k: _rounded(v) for k, v in value.items()}
728	    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
729	        return [_rounded(v) for v in value]
730	    return value
731	
732	
733	def write_figures(results: dict, inputs: dict[str, Path], out: Path) -> dict:
734	    """Every figure as a PNG in `out`, and figures.json: inputs with their SHA-256, files and checks."""
735	    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
736	    plt.rcParams.update(STYLE)
737	    entries = []
738	    for figure_id, (name, reads, draw) in FIGURES.items():
739	        data, checks = results[figure_id]
740	        fig = draw(data, checks)
741	        fig.savefig(out / name, dpi=DPI, metadata={"Software": None})
742	        plt.close(fig)
743	        entries.append({"id": figure_id, "file": name, "inputs": list(reads), "checks": _rounded(checks)})
744	    manifest = {
745	        "format": MANIFEST_FORMAT,
746	        "generator": "etf_risk.plots",
747	        "plots_py_sha256": digest(Path(__file__))["sha256"],
748	        "uv_lock_sha256": digest(REPO_ROOT / "uv.lock")["sha256"] if (REPO_ROOT / "uv.lock").is_file() else None,
749	        "matplotlib": matplotlib.__version__,
750	        "inputs": {name: {"path": shown_path(path), **digest(path)} for name, path in inputs.items()},
751	        "figures": entries,
752	    }
753	    (out / "figures.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
754	    return manifest
755	
756	
757	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
758	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
759	    parser.add_argument("--run", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_RUN, help="run folder (default: the run of record)")
760	    parser.add_argument("--snapshot", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT, help="processed data snapshot")
761	    parser.add_argument("--windows", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_WINDOWS, help="window definitions of the run")
762	    parser.add_argument("--experiments", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_EXPERIMENTS,
763	                        help="folder holding the experiments' measurement CSVs, as under data/ (default: data)")
764	    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT, help="folder for the figures and figures.json")
765	    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true",
766	                        help="print each figure's checked numbers and compare them with the documented values")
767	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
768	    inputs = default_inputs(args.run, args.snapshot, args.windows, args.experiments)
769	    results = compute(inputs)
770	    defaults = ((args.run, args.snapshot, args.windows, args.experiments)
771	                == (DEFAULT_RUN, DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT, DEFAULT_WINDOWS, DEFAULT_EXPERIMENTS))
772	    problems = compare_documented(results) if defaults else []
773	    if args.check:
774	        for figure_id, (_, checks) in results.items():
775	            print(f"{figure_id}: {json.dumps(_rounded(checks))}")
776	    else:
777	        manifest = write_figures(results, inputs, resolve(args.out))
778	        print(f"{len(manifest['figures'])} figures and figures.json -> {shown_path(resolve(args.out))}")
779	    if defaults:
780	        print("documented values: " + ("all match" if not problems else f"{len(problems)} differ"))
781	        for problem in problems:
782	            print(f"  {problem}")
783	    return 1 if problems else 0

"""Figures for the final write-up (Stage 4, docs/spec.md §4), drawn from result files only.

Run from the repository root (the plotting library is in the "plots" dependency group):

    uv run --group plots python -m etf_risk.plots
    uv run --group plots python -m etf_risk.plots --check

The first writes every figure and figures.json into docs/figures/; the second computes each figure's
checked numbers, compares them with the values the documents report (DOCUMENTED, used only with the
default inputs) and draws nothing. Both exit with 1 if a checked number differs from its documented
value. Every figure reads finished result files (Parquet, JSON, CSV) and recomputes nothing in Spark:

  M1-M5  the run of record, rolling-252-s21-r2, run-20261013T043848Z-2 (the protocol's four runs
         have identical tables): one panel per ticker, QQQ never pooled with the four stocks it
         holds, the overlapping windows labeled as such, windows that use an unverified extreme day
         marked, and the windows whose 2x path was breached shown on their own (M5)
  S1     the same run, over all windows and over the windows without an unverified day
  D1-D2  the data snapshot's daily returns and the run's window definitions
  X1-X4  the stride, shuffle-partition and caching experiments and the pandas baseline, from their
         measurements CSVs: each with its own time metric (wall_s, or wall_excl_capture_s where
         plans were recorded), its measured runs only, and its documented caveats in the note

Regenerating in the same fixed environment (this lockfile's packages, among them matplotlib and its
bundled DejaVu fonts, on the same platform) gives byte-identical files: the Agg backend, a fixed font,
size and DPI, no date or software metadata, and a manifest without timestamps. Another environment
may render the PNGs differently.

AI contribution: written with Claude Code (Opus 5.5). Verified with tests/test_plots.py and, on the
real data, by --check against the values in docs/spec.md §8 and the experiment documents.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import math
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")                          # no display: the same renderer on every machine
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt                # noqa: E402
import numpy as np                             # noqa: E402
import pandas as pd                            # noqa: E402
import pyarrow.parquet as pq                   # noqa: E402
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D             # noqa: E402
from matplotlib.ticker import PercentFormatter  # noqa: E402

from etf_risk.provenance import REPO_ROOT, resolve  # noqa: E402

SNAPSHOT = "full-2026-10-12"
DEFAULT_RUN = Path(f"data/outputs/windows/{SNAPSHOT}/rolling-252-s21-r2/run-20261013T043848Z-2")
DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT = Path(f"data/processed/{SNAPSHOT}")
DEFAULT_WINDOWS = Path(f"data/windows/{SNAPSHOT}/rolling-252-s21-r2")
DEFAULT_OUT = Path("docs/figures")
DEFAULT_EXPERIMENTS = Path("data")
EXPERIMENT_CSVS = {   # input name -> the experiment's measurements CSV, under the experiments root
    "stride_csv": Path("outputs-experiments/measurements.csv"),
    "partitions_csv": Path("outputs-partitions/batch-1/measurements.csv"),
    "baseline_csv": Path("outputs-baseline/batch-1/measurements.csv"),
    "caching_csv": Path("outputs-caching/batch-1/measurements.csv"),
}
PHASES = ("session_start", "window_stats_and_construction_check", "model_and_path_days", "summaries_and_pairing",
          "checks")
PHASE_LABELS = ("session\nstart", "window\nstatistics", "model and\npath_days", "summaries\nand pairing", "checks")
GROUP_COLORS = ("tab:blue", "tab:orange", "tab:green", "tab:purple")
TICKER_ORDER = ("AAPL", "MSFT", "NVDA", "TSLA", "QQQ")   # the spec's order: the four stocks, then QQQ
KEY = ["window_kind", "ticker", "window_days", "entry_date"]
BOUND_TOL = 1e-12                  # spark_pipeline.BOUND_TOL, the tolerance of the drawdown-bound check
MANIFEST_FORMAT = 1
DPI = 150
STYLE = {
    "font.family": "DejaVu Sans", "font.size": 8.5, "axes.titlesize": 8.5, "axes.labelsize": 8.5,
    "legend.fontsize": 7.5, "xtick.labelsize": 7.5, "ytick.labelsize": 7.5, "axes.spines.top": False,
    "axes.spines.right": False, "axes.grid": True, "grid.alpha": 0.3, "grid.linewidth": 0.5,
    "figure.dpi": DPI, "savefig.dpi": DPI,
}
PLAIN, FLAGGED, GUIDE = "tab:blue", "tab:orange", "0.3"
UNVERIFIED_RULE = ("Unverified extreme day: |daily return| ≥ 20%, a move over 15% reversed the next day by over "
                   "13%, or a split day with |return| ≥ 10%, not yet checked against a second source "
                   "(data-sources.md). The days are kept in the data.")


def overlap_note(unit: str = "panel") -> str:
    return ("Rolling 252-trading-day windows, a new one every 21 trading days, so the windows overlap. "
            f"One {unit} per ticker; QQQ holds the other four and is not pooled with them.")


def signed(value: float, digits: int = 1) -> str:
    """A percentage with its sign and a true minus sign, as the axes print it."""
    return f"{value:+.{digits}%}".replace("-", "−")


# --- inputs ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def read_table(path: Path, columns: list[str] | None = None, filters=None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """A Parquet file or table folder as pandas, with the ticker partition column as plain strings."""
    df = pq.read_table(path, columns=columns, filters=filters).to_pandas()
    if "ticker" in df.columns:
        df["ticker"] = df["ticker"].astype(str)
    return df


def tickers_in(values) -> list[str]:
    """The spec's ticker order, then any other ticker alphabetically (as in test data)."""
    present = set(values)
    return [t for t in TICKER_ORDER if t in present] + sorted(present - set(TICKER_ORDER))


def digest(path: Path) -> dict:
    """SHA-256 of a file, or of a folder's sorted (relative path, SHA-256) lines; with the file count."""
    if path.is_file():
        return {"sha256": hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), "files": 1}
    files = sorted(p for p in path.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and not p.name.startswith("."))
    lines = "".join(f"{p.relative_to(path).as_posix()} {hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}\n"
                    for p in files)
    return {"sha256": hashlib.sha256(lines.encode()).hexdigest(), "files": len(files)}


def shown_path(path: Path) -> str:
    """Repository-relative where possible, so no local path reaches a committed manifest."""
    try:
        return path.resolve().relative_to(REPO_ROOT).as_posix()
    except ValueError:
        return path.as_posix()


# --- figure data: (data, checks) ----------------------------------------------------------

def m1_returns(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """M1: 2x against 1x window returns. A breached 2x path has no 2x return, so it is left out."""
    both = paired.dropna(subset=["return_1x", "return_2x"])
    checks = {}
    for t in tickers_in(paired["ticker"]):
        w = both[both["ticker"] == t]
        checks[t] = {"windows_with_both_returns": int(len(w)),
                     "above_twice_1x": int((w["return_2x"] > 2 * w["return_1x"]).sum()),
                     "breached_2x": int((paired.loc[paired["ticker"] == t, "breached_2x"] == True).sum())}  # noqa: E712
    return both, checks


def m2_gap(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """M2: the exact log gap against its approximation −Σr² (expectation 1), windows without a breach."""
    ok = paired.dropna(subset=["exact_gap", "approx_gap"])
    checks = {"windows_without_breach": int(len(ok)),
              "largest_exact_gap": float(ok["exact_gap"].max()),
              "largest_identity_difference": float((ok["log_gap"] - ok["exact_gap"]).abs().max()),
              "median_relative_error": {t: float(ok.loc[ok["ticker"] == t, "approx_rel_error"].median())
                                        for t in tickers_in(ok["ticker"])}}
    return ok, checks


def m3_drawdown(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """M3: 2x against 1x maximum drawdown with the bound 1 − (1 − MDD_1x)² (expectation 2)."""
    ok = paired.dropna(subset=["mdd_1x", "mdd_2x", "mdd_bound"])
    below = ok["mdd_2x"] < ok["mdd_bound"] - BOUND_TOL
    checks = {t: {"windows": int((ok["ticker"] == t).sum()), "below_bound": int(below[ok["ticker"] == t].sum())}
              for t in tickers_in(ok["ticker"])}
    return ok, checks


def m4_turnover(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """M4: the 2x path's mean daily turnover per window (expectation 4); breached windows have none."""
    ok = paired.dropna(subset=["mean_turnover_2x"])
    checks = {t: {"windows": int((ok["ticker"] == t).sum()),
                  "median_mean_turnover_2x": float(ok.loc[ok["ticker"] == t, "mean_turnover_2x"].median())}
              for t in tickers_in(ok["ticker"])}
    return ok, checks


def m5_breaches(paired: pd.DataFrame, run: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """M5: the 2x NAV of every window whose 2x path was breached (expectation 3), from path_days."""
    breached = paired[paired["breached_2x"] == True]  # noqa: E712
    paths = []
    for t in tickers_in(breached["ticker"]):
        days = read_table(run / "path_days", columns=[*KEY, "leverage", "day", "date", "daily_return", "nav"],
                          filters=[("ticker", "=", t)])
        paths.append(days[days["leverage"] == 2.0].merge(breached.loc[breached["ticker"] == t, KEY], on=KEY))
    data = (pd.concat(paths, ignore_index=True) if paths
            else pd.DataFrame(columns=[*KEY, "leverage", "day", "date", "daily_return", "nav"]))
    breach_returns = sorted({float(r) for r in data.merge(
        breached[[*KEY, "breach_date_2x"]], on=KEY).query("date == breach_date_2x")["daily_return"]})
    checks = {"breached_windows": int(len(breached)), "tickers": tickers_in(breached["ticker"]),
              "breach_dates": sorted({str(d) for d in breached["breach_date_2x"]}),
              "breach_day_returns": breach_returns,
              "all_use_an_unverified_day": bool(breached["contains_unverified_day"].all())}
    return data, checks


def s1_sensitivity(paired: pd.DataFrame) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """S1: exact medians of the 1x and 2x returns over all windows and over the windows without an
    unverified day, as analysis/sql_sensitivity.py computes them for 2x (percentile 0.5, nulls left out)."""
    rows = []
    for t in tickers_in(paired["ticker"]):
        w = paired[paired["ticker"] == t]
        plain = w[w["contains_unverified_day"] == False]  # noqa: E712
        for leverage, column in (("1x", "return_1x"), ("2x", "return_2x")):
            rows.append({"ticker": t, "leverage": leverage,
                         "all_windows": int(w[column].count()), "all_median": float(w[column].median()),
                         "unflagged_windows": int(plain[column].count()),
                         "unflagged_median": float(plain[column].median()) if plain[column].count() else math.nan})
    data = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    checks = {f"{r.ticker} {r.leverage}": {"all_windows": r.all_windows, "all_median": r.all_median,
                                           "unflagged_windows": r.unflagged_windows,
                                           "unflagged_median": r.unflagged_median} for r in data.itertuples()}
    return data, checks


def d1_returns(snapshot: Path) -> tuple[tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame], dict]:
    """D1: every daily return of the snapshot, with the unverified extreme days of its quality report."""
    returns = pd.concat([read_table(f, columns=["ticker", "date", "daily_return"])
                         for f in sorted((snapshot / "daily_returns").glob("*.parquet"))], ignore_index=True)
    returns = returns.dropna(subset=["daily_return"])
    report = json.loads((snapshot / "quality_report.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    flagged = pd.DataFrame([{"ticker": d["ticker"], "date": pd.Timestamp(d["date"]).date()}
                            for d in report.get("unverified_extreme_days", [])], columns=["ticker", "date"])
    flagged = flagged.merge(returns, on=["ticker", "date"], how="left")
    checks = {"unverified_extreme_days": int(len(flagged)),
              "unverified_days_without_a_return": int(flagged["daily_return"].isna().sum())}
    for t in tickers_in(returns["ticker"]):
        r = returns[returns["ticker"] == t]
        checks[t] = {"returns": int(len(r)), "first_date": str(r["date"].min()), "last_date": str(r["date"].max()),
                     "unverified_extreme_days": int((flagged["ticker"] == t).sum())}
    return (returns, flagged), checks


def d2_windows(windows: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """D2: the entry date of every window definition, and whether it uses an unverified day."""
    config = json.loads((windows / "config.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    defs = read_table(windows / config["windows_file"], columns=[*KEY, "contains_unverified_day"])
    checks = {t: {"windows": int((defs["ticker"] == t).sum()),
                  "use_an_unverified_day": int(defs.loc[defs["ticker"] == t, "contains_unverified_day"].sum())}
              for t in tickers_in(defs["ticker"])}
    return defs, checks


def measured_runs(csv: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The runs an experiment's summaries use: not warm-ups, ended ok, and in a used protocol where the
    CSV marks one (the stride experiment's CSV does not)."""
    rows = pd.read_csv(csv)
    keep = (rows["warmup"] == False) & (rows["status"] == "ok")  # noqa: E712
    if "used" in rows:
        keep &= rows["used"] == True  # noqa: E712
    return rows[keep]


def summarize(rows: pd.DataFrame, by: str, metric: str) -> dict:
    """Per group, in order of first appearance: the runs, the experiment's own time metric (median and
    range), the phase medians, and peak total RSS in GiB (median and range)."""
    out = {}
    for key, g in rows.groupby(by, sort=False):
        peak = g["peak_rss_total_bytes"] / 2**30
        out[str(key)] = {"runs": int(len(g)), "metric": metric, "median_s": float(g[metric].median()),
                         "min_s": float(g[metric].min()), "max_s": float(g[metric].max()),
                         "phases_s": {p: float(g[f"{p}_s"].median()) if g[f"{p}_s"].notna().any() else math.nan
                                      for p in PHASES},              # pandas has no session start: undefined
                         "peak_median_gib": float(peak.median()), "peak_min_gib": float(peak.min()),
                         "peak_max_gib": float(peak.max())}
    return out


STRIDE_LABELS = {"baseline": "stride {}, first", "planned": "stride {}", "exploratory": "stride {}, exploratory",
                 "drift_check": "stride {}, repeated"}


def x1_stride(csv: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """X1: the stride experiment, per protocol in the order they ran; its time metric is wall_s (no plan
    capture). The repeated stride 21 is the drift check, and stride 3 is exploratory (experiments.md)."""
    rows = measured_runs(csv).sort_values(["protocol_id", "run_id"])
    rows = rows.assign(label=[STRIDE_LABELS[r.role].format(r.stride) for r in rows.itertuples()])
    protocols = summarize(rows, "label", "wall_s")
    for label, c in protocols.items():
        first = rows[rows["label"] == label].iloc[0]
        c.update({"protocol": str(first["protocol_id"]), "role": str(first["role"]), "stride": int(first["stride"]),
                  "windows": int(first["windows"])})
    baseline = next(c for c in protocols.values() if c["role"] == "baseline")
    repeated = next((c for c in protocols.values() if c["role"] == "drift_check"), None)
    drift = (repeated["median_s"] - baseline["median_s"]) / baseline["median_s"] if repeated else None
    return rows, {"protocols": protocols, "drift_of_the_repeated_protocol": drift}


def x2_partitions(csv: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """X2: the shuffle-partition experiment's configurations; time metric wall_excl_capture_s."""
    rows = measured_runs(csv)
    return rows, summarize(rows, "config", "wall_excl_capture_s")


def x3_baseline(csv: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """X3: the pandas baseline's implementations S and P; time metric wall_s (no plan capture)."""
    rows = measured_runs(csv)
    return rows, summarize(rows, "engine", "wall_s")


def x4_caching(csv: Path) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, dict]:
    """X4: the caching experiment's configurations; time metric wall_excl_capture_s."""
    rows = measured_runs(csv)
    return rows, summarize(rows, "config", "wall_excl_capture_s")


# --- drawing ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _panels(n: int, row_height: float = 2.9):
    """One axes per ticker, three to a row; a spare axes, if any, holds the legend."""
    cols = min(n, 3)
    rows = math.ceil(n / cols)
    fig, grid = plt.subplots(rows, cols, figsize=(3.6 * cols + 0.4, row_height * rows + 0.9), squeeze=False)
    axes = list(grid.ravel())
    for spare in axes[n:]:
        spare.axis("off")
    return fig, axes[:n], (axes[n] if len(axes) > n else None)


def _finish(fig, title: str, note: str | None = None, xlabel: str | None = None, ylabel: str | None = None,
            legend_from=None, legend_in=None, legend_on_top: bool = False) -> None:
    """Title, shared axis labels, legend and footnote, with room for each measured in inches. The legend
    goes into `legend_in` (a spare axes), into a band under the title (`legend_on_top`), or where it fits."""
    height = fig.get_figheight()
    note_room = 0.36 if note else 0.0              # up to two lines of 7-point text
    label_room = 0.32 if xlabel else 0.0
    top_room = 0.36 + (0.3 if legend_on_top else 0.0)
    fig.suptitle(title, x=0.01, ha="left", fontsize=10, fontweight="bold")
    if legend_from is not None:
        handles, labels = legend_from.get_legend_handles_labels()
        if legend_on_top:
            fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.01, 1 - 0.4 / height),
                       ncol=len(labels), frameon=False)
        else:
            (legend_in or legend_from).legend(handles, labels, loc="center" if legend_in else "best", frameon=False)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0.03 if ylabel else 0, (note_room + label_room) / height, 1, 1 - top_room / height))
    if xlabel:
        fig.supxlabel(xlabel, y=(note_room + 0.05) / height, va="bottom", fontsize=8.5)
    if ylabel:
        fig.supylabel(ylabel, x=0.004, ha="left", fontsize=8.5)
    if note:
        fig.text(0.01, 0.06 / height, note, fontsize=7, color="0.35", ha="left", va="bottom", wrap=True)


def _percent(ax, x: bool = True, y: bool = True) -> None:
    if x:
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1.0, decimals=0))
    if y:
        ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1.0, decimals=0))


def _by_flag(ax, w: pd.DataFrame, x: str, y: str) -> None:
    for flag, color, label in ((False, PLAIN, "window without an unverified day"),
                               (True, FLAGGED, "window that uses an unverified day")):
        part = w[w["contains_unverified_day"] == flag]
        ax.scatter(part[x], part[y], s=5, color=color, alpha=0.55, linewidths=0, label=f"{label}")


def draw_m1(data: pd.DataFrame, checks: dict):
    tickers = list(checks)
    fig, axes, spare = _panels(len(tickers))
    for ax, t in zip(axes, tickers):
        w, c = data[data["ticker"] == t], checks[t]
        _by_flag(ax, w, "return_1x", "return_2x")
        xs = np.array([w["return_1x"].min(), w["return_1x"].max()]) if len(w) else np.array([0.0, 0.0])
        ax.plot(xs, 2 * xs, color=GUIDE, lw=0.9, ls="--", label="twice the 1x return")
        ax.set_title(f"{t}: 2x above the line in {c['above_twice_1x']} of {c['windows_with_both_returns']}")
        if c["breached_2x"]:
            ax.text(0.03, 0.97, f"{c['breached_2x']} windows with a breached 2x path not shown (M5)",
                    transform=ax.transAxes, va="top", fontsize=6.5, color="0.35")
        _percent(ax)
    _finish(fig, "M1  The 2x window return against twice the 1x return", note=overlap_note(),
            xlabel="1x window return", ylabel="2x window return", legend_from=axes[0], legend_in=spare)
    return fig


def draw_m2(data: pd.DataFrame, checks: dict):
    tickers = list(checks["median_relative_error"])
    fig, axes, spare = _panels(len(tickers))
    for ax, t in zip(axes, tickers):
        w = data[data["ticker"] == t]
        _by_flag(ax, w, "approx_gap", "exact_gap")
        lo = min(w["approx_gap"].min(), w["exact_gap"].min()) if len(w) else 0.0
        ax.plot([lo, 0], [lo, 0], color=GUIDE, lw=0.9, ls="--", label=r"exact gap $= -\sum r^2$")
        ax.set_title(f"{t}: {len(w)} windows, median error {signed(checks['median_relative_error'][t])}")
    _finish(fig, "M2  The 2x log gap against minus the realized variance (windows without a breach)",
            note=overlap_note() + " Error: (−Σr² − exact gap) / |exact gap|.",
            xlabel=r"$-\sum r^2$, minus the window's realized variance",
            ylabel=r"exact log gap $\log(1+R_{2x}) - 2\,\log(1+R_{1x})$", legend_from=axes[0], legend_in=spare)
    return fig

            ax.plot([last, breach], [path["nav"][defined].iloc[-1], 0], lw=0.6, ls=":", color=FLAGGED)

def draw_x1(data: pd.DataFrame, checks: dict):
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9.6, 3.9))

              "exploratory": ("D", "0.4", False, "stride 3: exploratory only")}
    for c in checks["protocols"].values():
        marker, color, filled, _ = styles[c["role"]]
        for ax, mid, lo, hi in ((axes[0], c["median_s"], c["min_s"], c["max_s"]),
                                (axes[1], c["peak_median_gib"], c["peak_min_gib"], c["peak_max_gib"])):
            ax.errorbar([c["windows"]], [mid], yerr=[[mid - lo], [hi - mid]], fmt=marker, color=color, ms=5,

    drift = checks["drift_of_the_repeated_protocol"]
    _finish(fig, "X1  Stride experiment: runtime and peak memory against the number of windows",
            note="Three measured runs per protocol; time is wall_s (no plan capture). Drift detected: the repeated "
                 f"stride-21 median was {signed(drift)} against the first, outside the ±10% tolerance, so the "
                 "comparisons across strides are marked as affected. Stride 3 was not admitted by the experiment's "
                 "memory rule and is exploratory only (experiments.md).")
    return fig


def _draw_groups(checks: dict, labels: dict[str, str], title: str, metric: str, note: str):
    """Medians and ranges of the experiment's time metric and peak memory, and the phase medians, per group."""
    keys = list(checks)
    colors = dict(zip(keys, GROUP_COLORS))
    fig, (ax_t, ax_p, ax_m) = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(11.6, 3.9), gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [1, 2.3, 1]})
    x = np.arange(len(keys))
    for ax, (mid, lo, hi), fmt in ((ax_t, ("median_s", "min_s", "max_s"), "{:.1f} s"),
                                   (ax_m, ("peak_median_gib", "peak_min_gib", "peak_max_gib"), "{:.2f} GiB")):
        mids, los, his = (np.array([checks[k][f] for k in keys]) for f in (mid, lo, hi))
        ax.bar(x, mids, yerr=[mids - los, his - mids], color=[colors[k] for k in keys], width=0.6, capsize=3,
               error_kw={"lw": 0.9})
        for xi, m, h in zip(x, mids, his):        # the median's label sits above the range, not on it
            ax.annotate(fmt.format(m), (xi, h), xytext=(0, 3), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=7)
        ax.margins(y=0.12)
        ax.set_xticks(x, [labels[k] for k in keys])
    ax_t.set_ylabel(f"{metric} (s): median and range")
    ax_m.set_ylabel("peak total RSS (GiB): median and range")
    width = 0.8 / len(keys)
    for i, k in enumerate(keys):
        values = [checks[k]["phases_s"][p] for p in PHASES]
        ax_p.bar(np.arange(len(PHASES)) + (i - (len(keys) - 1) / 2) * width, values, width=width, color=colors[k],
                 label=labels[k].replace("\n", " "))
    ax_p.set_xticks(np.arange(len(PHASES)), PHASE_LABELS)
    ax_p.set_ylabel("phase time (s): median")
    ax_p.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=7)
    _finish(fig, title, note=note)
    return fig

def compare_documented(results: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Every difference between the checked numbers and DOCUMENTED (for the default inputs only)."""
    doc, problems = DOCUMENTED, []

    def same(label, got, want):
        if got != want:
            problems.append(f"{label}: {got}, documented {want}")

    def pct(value):
        return None if value is None else round(100 * value, 1)

    m1, m2, m3, m4, m5 = (results[k][1] for k in ("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5"))
    s1, d1, d2 = results["S1"][1], results["D1"][1], results["D2"][1]
    for t, n in doc["windows"].items():           # a ticker missing from the results is a difference, not an error
        d2t, m1t, m3t = d2.get(t, {}), m1.get(t, {}), m3.get(t, {})
        s1x, s2x = s1.get(f"{t} 1x", {}), s1.get(f"{t} 2x", {})
        same(f"D2 {t} windows", d2t.get("windows"), n)
        same(f"D2 {t} windows with an unverified day", d2t.get("use_an_unverified_day"),
             doc["windows_with_an_unverified_day"][t])
        same(f"M1 {t} above twice the 1x return", (m1t.get("above_twice_1x"), m1t.get("windows_with_both_returns")),
             doc["above_twice_1x"][t])
        same(f"M3 {t} windows below the bound", m3t.get("below_bound"), 0)
        same(f"S1 {t} median 1x return", pct(s1x.get("all_median")), doc["median_return_1x_percent"][t])
        same(f"S1 {t} median 2x return and windows", (pct(s2x.get("all_median")), s2x.get("all_windows")),
             doc["median_return_2x_percent"][t])
    tsla = s1.get("TSLA 2x", {})
    same("S1 TSLA 2x median and windows without an unverified day",
         (pct(tsla.get("unflagged_median")), tsla.get("unflagged_windows")), doc["tsla_2x_unflagged"])
    same("M2 windows without a breach", m2["windows_without_breach"], doc["windows_without_breach"])
    same("M2 largest exact gap is at most 0", m2["largest_exact_gap"] <= 0, True)
    errors = m2["median_relative_error"]
    same("M2 lowest and highest median relative error",
         ((round(100 * min(errors.values()), 1), min(errors, key=errors.get)),
          (round(100 * max(errors.values()), 1), max(errors, key=errors.get))), doc["median_relative_error_range"])
    turnover = {t: c["median_mean_turnover_2x"] for t, c in m4.items()}
    same("M4 lowest and highest median turnover",
         ((round(100 * min(turnover.values()), 1), min(turnover, key=turnover.get)),
          (round(100 * max(turnover.values()), 1), max(turnover, key=turnover.get))), doc["median_turnover_range"])
    same("M5 breaches", {"windows": m5["breached_windows"], "tickers": m5["tickers"], "dates": m5["breach_dates"],
                         "returns_percent": [round(100 * r, 1) for r in m5["breach_day_returns"]]}, doc["breaches"])
    same("M5 every breached window uses an unverified day", m5["all_use_an_unverified_day"], True)
    same("D1 unverified extreme days", d1["unverified_extreme_days"], doc["unverified_extreme_days"])
    same("D1 unverified days without a return", d1["unverified_days_without_a_return"], 0)
    groups = {"X1": results["X1"][1]["protocols"], **{k: results[k][1] for k in ("X2", "X3", "X4")}}
    for figure_id, documented in ((k, doc[k]) for k in ("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4")):
        for group, values in documented.items():
            c = groups[figure_id].get(group, {})
            same(f"{figure_id} {group} median time and peak",
                 (three_decimals(c.get("median_s")), three_decimals(c.get("peak_median_gib"))), values)
    drift = results["X1"][1]["drift_of_the_repeated_protocol"]
    same("X1 drift of the repeated stride 21", pct(drift), doc["X1_drift_percent"])
    return problems


def three_decimals(value):
    """A number rounded as the experiment documents report it: three decimals."""
    return None if value is None else round(value, 3)


def _rounded(value):
    if isinstance(value, float):
        return None if math.isnan(value) else round(value, 6)
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {k: _rounded(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [_rounded(v) for v in value]
    return value


def write_figures(results: dict, inputs: dict[str, Path], out: Path) -> dict:
    """Every figure as a PNG in `out`, and figures.json: inputs with their SHA-256, files and checks."""
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    plt.rcParams.update(STYLE)
    entries = []
    for figure_id, (name, reads, draw) in FIGURES.items():
        data, checks = results[figure_id]
        fig = draw(data, checks)
        fig.savefig(out / name, dpi=DPI, metadata={"Software": None})
        plt.close(fig)
        entries.append({"id": figure_id, "file": name, "inputs": list(reads), "checks": _rounded(checks)})
    manifest = {
        "format": MANIFEST_FORMAT,
        "generator": "etf_risk.plots",
        "plots_py_sha256": digest(Path(__file__))["sha256"],
        "uv_lock_sha256": digest(REPO_ROOT / "uv.lock")["sha256"] if (REPO_ROOT / "uv.lock").is_file() else None,
        "matplotlib": matplotlib.__version__,
        "inputs": {name: {"path": shown_path(path), **digest(path)} for name, path in inputs.items()},
        "figures": entries,
    }
    (out / "figures.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return manifest


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--run", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_RUN, help="run folder (default: the run of record)")
    parser.add_argument("--snapshot", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT, help="processed data snapshot")
    parser.add_argument("--windows", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_WINDOWS, help="window definitions of the run")
    parser.add_argument("--experiments", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_EXPERIMENTS,
                        help="folder holding the experiments' measurement CSVs, as under data/ (default: data)")
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT, help="folder for the figures and figures.json")
    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true",
                        help="print each figure's checked numbers and compare them with the documented values")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    inputs = default_inputs(args.run, args.snapshot, args.windows, args.experiments)
    results = compute(inputs)
    defaults = ((args.run, args.snapshot, args.windows, args.experiments)
                == (DEFAULT_RUN, DEFAULT_SNAPSHOT, DEFAULT_WINDOWS, DEFAULT_EXPERIMENTS))
    problems = compare_documented(results) if defaults else []
    if args.check:
        for figure_id, (_, checks) in results.items():
            print(f"{figure_id}: {json.dumps(_rounded(checks))}")
    else:
        manifest = write_figures(results, inputs, resolve(args.out))
        print(f"{len(manifest['figures'])} figures and figures.json -> {shown_path(resolve(args.out))}")
    if defaults:
        print("documented values: " + ("all match" if not problems else f"{len(problems)} differ"))
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"  {problem}")
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	# Leveraged ETF Risk Analytics
2	
3	How does a fund that resets to twice its underlying every trading day behave
4	over a one-year holding period, compared with the underlying and with twice its
5	return? This CS544 independent project replays a daily-reset 1x/2x model on the
6	daily return history of NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, TSLA and QQQ over 252-trading-day
7	windows, runs it in PySpark with full-scale checks, and analyzes the results
8	with Spark SQL. The results describe historical windows of a few tickers; they
9	are not forecasts, and the model ignores fees, financing and execution.
10	
11	## Status
12	
13	| Part | Status |
14	|---|---|
15	| Data: download with manifest, checksum-enforced ingest, validation, daily returns in Parquet | Implemented |
16	| Model and Spark pipeline: 252-day windows on a shared trading-day grid, 1x and 2x for each window, full-scale checks, an independent sample check, measurement tooling | Implemented |
17	| Three Spark SQL analyses of the results ([`analysis/`](analysis/)) | Implemented |
18	| Docker image for the pipeline | Implemented |
19	| Stride experiment: runtime and memory at strides 21, 14 and 7 ([docs/experiments.md](docs/experiments.md)) | Complete; drift detected, stride 3 exploratory only |
20	| Shuffle-partition experiment: three Spark partition settings at stride 7 ([docs/partition-experiment.md](docs/partition-experiment.md)) | Complete; B (200 partitions, coalescing off) slower than A and C; no clear memory difference; outputs within tolerance |
21	| Pandas baseline: the Spark pipeline against a single-process pandas implementation, end to end, at stride 7 ([docs/pandas-baseline.md](docs/pandas-baseline.md)) | Complete; pandas had a 41.8% shorter median wall time and a 26.6% lower median peak total RSS; outputs within tolerance |
22	| Caching experiment: no cache, the window-member rows, and those plus the four read-back tables, at stride 7 ([docs/caching-experiment.md](docs/caching-experiment.md)) | Complete; no clear difference in runtime or peak memory; outputs within tolerance |
23	| Figures and final write-up | Planned |
24	| Optional systems extension: MySQL job table, Kafka job queue, Redis result cache | Planned ([spec](docs/spec.md), §11) |
25	
26	## Reading guide
27	
28	1. **This README**: status, key results and how to run everything.
29	2. **[docs/spec.md](docs/spec.md)**: the research questions (§2), the model and
30	   its assumptions (§3), how results are checked (§6), the window design (§7),
31	   the full results of the stride-21 run and summaries of the stride,
32	   shuffle-partition and caching experiments and the pandas baseline (§8).
33	3. **[docs/data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md)**: where the data comes from,
34	   the checks run on it, and what is not verified.
35	4. **[docs/experiments.md](docs/experiments.md)**: the stride experiment, with
36	   its design and predictions (committed before any measured run), run log,
37	   deviations, measurements and answers;
38	   [`collect_measurements.py`](analysis/collect_measurements.py) builds its
39	   measurements CSV from the run records.
40	5. **[docs/partition-experiment.md](docs/partition-experiment.md)**: the
41	   shuffle-partition experiment, with its design, rules and predictions
42	   (committed before any measured run), run log, deviations, measurements,
43	   plans and answers; the [session helpers](docs/partition-session.zsh) ran
44	   its session, and the [collector](analysis/collect_partition_measurements.py)
45	   builds its measurements CSV and checks its acceptance criteria.
46	6. **[docs/pandas-baseline.md](docs/pandas-baseline.md)**: the pandas
47	   baseline, an end-to-end comparison of the Spark pipeline with a
48	   single-process pandas implementation of the same computation, with its
49	   design, rules and predictions (committed before any measured run), run log,
50	   measurements and answers; the [session helpers](docs/baseline-session.zsh)
51	   ran its session, and the
52	   [collector](analysis/collect_baseline_measurements.py) builds its
53	   measurements CSV and checks its acceptance criteria.
54	7. **[docs/caching-experiment.md](docs/caching-experiment.md)**: the caching
55	   experiment, which compared no cache, a cache of the window-member rows, and
56	   one of those rows plus the four read-back tables, with its design, rules and
57	   predictions (committed before any measured run), run log, measurements,
58	   cache checks and answers; the [session helpers](docs/caching-session.zsh)
59	   ran its session, and the
60	   [collector](analysis/collect_caching_measurements.py) builds its
61	   measurements CSV and checks its acceptance criteria.
62	8. **The analyses**: [`sql_overview.py`](analysis/sql_overview.py) (counts and
63	   medians per ticker), [`sql_comparison.py`](analysis/sql_comparison.py) (how
64	   often 2x beats twice the 1x return) and
65	   [`sql_sensitivity.py`](analysis/sql_sensitivity.py) (medians without the
66	   windows that use an unverified day).
67	9. **The code**, in data-flow order: in `src/etf_risk/`, `download` → `ingest`
68	   (with `validate`) → `windows` → `spark_pipeline` (which runs `model`) →
69	   `verify`; `measure` times runs, `plans` records a run's execution plans,
70	   and `pandas_pipeline` computes the same results in one process without
71	   Spark. Module overview: spec §5.
72	10. **How AI was used**: [AI assistance](#ai-assistance) below.
73	
74	## Key results
75	
76	From the run of record: snapshot `full-2026-10-12` (daily history through
77	2025-12-31), 252-day windows starting every 21 trading days. The windows
78	overlap, so these numbers describe one history, not independent samples; spec
79	§8 has the details.
80	
81	- All 46 check tests passed with no violation on 1,790 windows, and the
82	  independent Python check matched all 1,074 paths it compared. Every window
83	  without a breach (1,778) passes the two identity checks of the 2x model (exact
84	  log gap, drawdown bound).
85	- 12 AAPL windows breach at 2x (a daily loss of 50% or more); all contain
86	  2000-09-29, a day not yet checked against a second source. They have no 2x
87	  return and are left out of the 2x statistics below.
88	
89	| | AAPL | MSFT | NVDA | TSLA | QQQ |
90	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
91	| Windows | 529 | 466 | 311 | 174 | 310 |
92	| Median 1x return | 24.4% | 22.8% | 39.5% | 22.5% | 16.6% |
93	| Median 2x return | 35.2% (517 windows) | 39.9% | 51.3% | 13.5% | 31.4% |
94	| 2x return above twice the 1x return | 219 of 517 (42.4%) | 164 of 466 (35.2%) | 141 of 311 (45.3%) | 43 of 174 (24.7%) | 140 of 310 (45.2%) |
95	| Windows using an unverified extreme day | 78 | 12 | 92 | 57 | 0 |
96	| Median 2x return without those windows | 48.5% (451) | 41.4% (454) | 52.2% (219) | −12.3% (117) | 31.4% (310) |
97	
98	- For every ticker, the daily-reset 2x return exceeded twice the 1x return in
99	  fewer than half of the windows.
100	- The last row is a sensitivity analysis: TSLA's 2x median falls from 13.5% to
101	  −12.3%, while AAPL's rises from 35.2% to 48.5%. It shows how much a result
102	  depends on periods with extreme days, not whether those days are data errors.
103	- Runtime and memory were measured on one Apple Silicon laptop (8 cores, 8 GiB
104	  RAM), with Spark in local mode and, apart from the shuffle-partition
105	  experiment, default settings; the numbers describe that machine and those
106	  configurations, not others. For the run of record, the median wall time over
107	  three measured runs was 44.7 s and the median peak memory 1.27 GiB (summed
108	  resident memory of the run's processes, sampled every 0.25 s).
109	- The stride experiment ([docs/experiments.md](docs/experiments.md)) measured
110	  the same stride-21 workload and strides 14 and 7 (1.5 and 3 times the
111	  windows) on 2026-10-19: median wall times 22.2, 20.3 and 25.7 s, median
112	  peaks 2.62 to 2.70 GiB, and every check passed in all 20 runs. At stride 21
113	  that is half the run of record's time and about twice its memory, with more
114	  memory free before the runs; the records do not establish why. A linear fit
115	  over the three strides gives an intercept of 18.8 s (85% of the stride-21
116	  median) and 1.2 ms per window: an estimate from three points, not measured
117	  overhead. A repeated stride-21 protocol at the end had an 18.3% shorter
118	  median wall time than the first, beyond the 10% drift tolerance, so
119	  comparisons across strides are marked as affected. Stride 3 was run although
120	  the experiment's memory rule did not admit it; its results (40.2 s,
121	  2.73 GiB) are exploratory only.
122	- The shuffle-partition experiment
123	  ([docs/partition-experiment.md](docs/partition-experiment.md)) ran the
124	  stride-7 workload on 2026-10-22 (UTC) with three settings: A, Spark's
125	  defaults (200 shuffle partitions, AQE coalescing on); B, 200 partitions with
126	  coalescing off; C, 8 partitions with coalescing off. Eight runs each, in the
127	  order A–B–C–C–B–A, all passed every check. Median times without the plan
128	  recording were 26.5, 44.6 and 25.3 s: B's was 69% longer than A's and 77%
129	  longer than C's, in the same direction in both halves of the order, while A
130	  and C showed no clear difference. Median peaks were 2.69 GiB in all three,
131	  and `paired` and `path_summary` matched A's within the tolerance. In B, one
132	  join stayed a sort-merge join where AQE chose a broadcast join in A and C.
133	  No drift was detected; the machine checks were recorded only before the
134	  first protocol, and the last protocol followed a two-hour break.
135	- The pandas baseline
136	  ([docs/pandas-baseline.md](docs/pandas-baseline.md)) compared the Spark
137	  pipeline at Spark's defaults end to end with a single-process pandas
138	  implementation of the same computation, on the stride-7 workload on
139	  2026-10-22 (UTC): eight runs each, in the order Spark–pandas–pandas–Spark,
140	  all passing every check. The pandas implementation's median wall time was
141	  15.4 s against Spark's 26.4 s (41.8% shorter), and its median peak total RSS
142	  1.97 against 2.68 GiB (26.6% lower), in the same direction in both halves of
143	  the order; its outputs matched Spark's within the tolerance. Its model phase
144	  took longer than Spark's and its other phases less time. Both call the same
145	  model function but handle data, aggregate and write in their own ways, so
146	  the comparison does not isolate Spark's overhead. The prediction had put
147	  pandas at about 40 s, slower than Spark; no drift was detected.
148	- The caching experiment
149	  ([docs/caching-experiment.md](docs/caching-experiment.md)) ran the stride-7
150	  workload on 2026-10-22 (UTC) with three caching strategies: A, no cache; B,
151	  the window-member rows cached from the window statistics through the model
152	  phase; C, those rows and the four tables read back after each phase, cached
153	  through the checks. Eight runs each, in the order A–B–C–C–B–A, all passed
154	  every check, and Spark's storage information and the execution plans
155	  verified every cache's fill and release and the cached reads in each phase.
156	  Median times without the plan recording were 26.5, 27.0 and 28.7 s: B's and
157	  C's were 2.1% and 8.4% longer than A's, below the 10% threshold, so there was
158	  no clear difference. Caching the members lengthened the window statistics by
159	  0.9 s and shortened the model phase by 0.3 s; C's further caches lengthened
160	  the model phase by 1.3 s, with no observed net saving in the later phases.
161	  Median peaks were 2.68–2.70 GiB, with C's caches, about 0.2 GiB, held in the
162	  JVM heap. All outputs matched A's within the tolerance; in B and C, seven
163	  floating-point summary columns differed in the last bits, and a different
164	  order of addition is a plausible but unestablished explanation. No drift was
165	  detected.
166	
167	## Running
168	
169	Requires Python 3.12, Java 17 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/); run the
170	commands from the repository root. Memory use has been measured on one machine
171	only (see Key results): there, runs at strides 21 to 7 peaked at 1.2 to 2.8 GiB,
172	and the exploratory stride-3 runs at up to 2.8 GiB; other machines, and Spark
173	settings beyond the shuffle-partition experiment's three, have not been
174	measured.
175	
176	```bash
177	uv sync                                    # .venv from uv.lock
178	uv run --group measure pytest              # tests, no network
179	
180	# 1. Download a snapshot (network). Set SNAPSHOT once; the later steps use it.
181	SNAPSHOT=full-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
182	uv run --group download python -m etf_risk.download \
183	    --tickers NVDA AAPL MSFT TSLA QQQ --out data/raw/yahoo/$SNAPSHOT
184	# 2. Check the prices, then write daily returns       -> data/processed/$SNAPSHOT/
185	uv run python -m etf_risk.ingest --raw-dir data/raw/yahoo/$SNAPSHOT
186	# 3. Define 252-day windows at stride 21              -> data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21/
187	uv run python -m etf_risk.windows --snapshot $SNAPSHOT --kind rolling --stride 21
188	# 4. Run the model in Spark; every check runs at full scale -> $RUN
189	RUN=data/outputs/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21/first
190	uv run python -m etf_risk.spark_pipeline --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21 --run-id first
191	# 5. Compare a sample of windows with an independent Python computation
192	uv run python -m etf_risk.verify --run $RUN
193	# 6. The three SQL analyses of the run
194	uv run python analysis/sql_overview.py $RUN
195	uv run python analysis/sql_comparison.py $RUN
196	uv run python analysis/sql_sensitivity.py $RUN
197	```
198	
199	Optional steps, with the same variables:
200	
201	```bash
202	# Calendar-year windows, a labeled supplement
203	uv run python -m etf_risk.windows --snapshot $SNAPSHOT --kind calendar-year
204	uv run python -m etf_risk.spark_pipeline --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/calendar-year --run-id first
205	# Timed runs with peak memory: a fresh process per run; no further run once 60% of RAM is crossed
206	uv run --group measure python -m etf_risk.measure --repeats 4 -- --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21
207	```
208	
209	- Unless `--end` is changed, the download stops at 2025-12-31, the same range as
210	  the run of record. Yahoo can revise adjusted prices, so a new snapshot can
211	  differ slightly ([data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md)).
212	- Nothing is overwritten: `windows` refuses an existing folder (unless
213	  `--overwrite`), and `spark_pipeline` asks for a new `--run-id`.
214	- `spark_pipeline` also takes `--shuffle-partitions N` and `--coalesce on|off`
215	  (Spark settings, refused inside an existing Spark session) and
216	  `--record-plans`, which writes `plans.json` with the run's final plans and
217	  the partition counts Spark used
218	  ([partition-experiment.md](docs/partition-experiment.md) 4).
219	- `spark_pipeline --cache none|members|members-checks` caches the
220	  window-member rows, or those and the four read-back tables, and records the
221	  fills, releases and Spark's storage information in `run.json`
222	  ([caching-experiment.md](docs/caching-experiment.md) 4).
223	- `etf_risk.pandas_pipeline` takes `--windows`, `--out-root` and `--run-id`
224	  and writes the Spark pipeline's outputs from one process, without Spark;
225	  `etf_risk.measure --pipeline pandas` times it
226	  ([pandas-baseline.md](docs/pandas-baseline.md) 4).
227	- Strides below 21 need `--allow-dense-stride`. Strides 14, 7 and 3 were
228	  measured in the stride experiment (stride 3 as exploratory only); stride 1
229	  has not been run.
230	- The 2020–2025 prototype regression needs the prototype CSVs, which were
231	  downloaded outside this repository ([data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md)).
232	
233	### Docker
234	
235	The image holds the code, Python 3.12, Java 17 and the locked dependencies. Data
236	is never copied into it: `docker/run.sh` mounts `data/processed` and
237	`data/windows` read-only and writes container results to `data/outputs-docker`
238	and `data/windows-docker`, apart from native results. Keep the image local; do
239	not push it.
240	
241	```bash
242	docker/build.sh            # builds etf-risk:dev; records the commit and whether src/, pyproject.toml, uv.lock were clean
243	docker/run.sh              # the test suite in the container (the transcript-hook tests stay native)
244	# Steps 4-5 in the container, on the definitions from step 3
245	docker/run.sh python -m etf_risk.spark_pipeline --windows data/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21 \
246	    --out-root data/outputs-docker/windows --run-id first
247	docker/run.sh python -m etf_risk.verify --run data/outputs-docker/windows/$SNAPSHOT/rolling-252-s21/first
248	```
249	
250	The SQL analyses run natively on a container run's folder as well. The image
251	has no `.git`, so run records take the commit and clean flag from the build
252	(`code_source: "build"`) and the image ID from `docker/run.sh`; `source_sha256`
253	still identifies the code. `docker/run.sh` sets a memory limit
254	(`ETF_RISK_MEMORY`, default `2.5g`, a budget to validate) with no swap and
255	prints the container's cgroup memory peak, which includes page cache. Timings
256	in the container (a Linux VM on macOS, data on bind mounts) are a separate
257	configuration, not comparable with native measurements.
258	
259	## Data
260	
261	Daily prices come from Yahoo Finance through yfinance and are not committed
262	(`data/` is gitignored; the data's terms of use have not been reviewed). The
263	run of record uses the full history of NVDA, AAPL, MSFT, TSLA and QQQ through
264	2025-12-31 (snapshot `full-2026-10-12`); a 2020–2025 snapshot of the four
265	stocks was used for the prototype. Download settings, dates, checksums, the
266	checks run, and open limitations are in [docs/data-sources.md](docs/data-sources.md).
267	
268	**Data status: partially checked, not fully verified.** Trading dates match
269	the NYSE schedule, and Adj Close is consistent with Yahoo's own dividend
270	records. For splits, none of the 23 split-day returns resembles an unadjusted
271	split; this does not independently prove that every split adjustment is
272	correct. A second-source comparison and a terms-of-use review have not been
273	done, and 36 extreme price moves, including AAPL on 2000-09-29, are
274	**unverified**.
275	
276	## Course concepts
277	
278	- **Python**: a sequential reference model with hand-calculated tests, and the
279	  data checks.
280	- **PyArrow and Parquet**: daily returns, window definitions and results with
281	  explicit schemas.
282	- **PySpark and Spark SQL**: grouped pandas functions and a broadcast join over
283	  every window; DataFrame aggregation and three SQL analyses; execution plans
284	  read with `explain("formatted")`.
285	- **Docker**: an image that reproduces the native results exactly on this
286	  project's machine.
287	- **Performance measurement**: fresh-process runs with memory sampling and a
288	  stop rule; a stride experiment whose design and predictions were committed
289	  before any measured run; a shuffle-partition experiment, likewise committed
290	  in advance, that compared three partition settings and recorded the
291	  partition counts Spark used; a pandas baseline, committed the same way, that
292	  compared the Spark pipeline end to end with a single-process pandas
293	  implementation; and a caching experiment, committed the same way, that
294	  compared three caching strategies and checked every cache in Spark's storage
295	  information and execution plans.
296	
297	## AI assistance
298	
299	Most of the code, tests and documentation were written with Claude Code (Opus
300	5.5) in reviewable stages. I set the requirements and constraints of each
301	stage, made the design decisions (often choosing among options Claude Code
302	proposed), reviewed results and diffs, and approved each commit. Each file
303	written or drafted with AI says so in its header (`AI contribution: ...`),
304	together with how it was checked.
305	
306	- **Written by me:** the breach branch of `simulate_path()` in
307	  `src/etf_risk/model.py`, and the SQL queries in `analysis/`. The queries were
308	  tutored exercises: Claude Code set the tasks and acceptance criteria and
309	  reviewed my attempts and my reading of the execution plan, without writing
310	  the queries. It later added the scripts' command-line input.
311	- **Other tools:** the transcript hook (`.claude/hooks/save_transcript.py`) was
312	  first drafted with Codex assistance, inspired by a `log_ai.py` script from a
313	  CS639 project; Claude Code later changed it to save one log per message and
314	  wrote its redaction module. The 2020–2025 prototype data was downloaded by a
315	  check written with Codex assistance outside this repository.
316	- **Records:** `docs/ai-usage/` holds redacted per-message transcripts of the
317	  Claude Code sessions, which I review before committing them
318	  ([docs/ai-usage/README.md](docs/ai-usage/README.md)). The hook does not commit
319	  or push files and has been checked against real sessions; conversations with
320	  other AI tools are not recorded.
321	
322	## Next steps
323	
324	1. **Performance experiments** (mine): the stride, shuffle-partition and
325	   caching experiments and the pandas baseline are complete
326	   ([docs/experiments.md](docs/experiments.md),
327	   [docs/partition-experiment.md](docs/partition-experiment.md),
328	   [docs/pandas-baseline.md](docs/pandas-baseline.md),
329	   [docs/caching-experiment.md](docs/caching-experiment.md)).
330	2. **Data**: compare the 36 unverified extreme days with a second source, and
331	   review the data's terms of use.
332	3. **Figures and the final write-up** (Stage 4).
333	4. **Optional systems extension** (spec §11): Docker Compose with MySQL, Kafka
334	   and Redis for a job queue and a result cache, with recovery and caching
335	   experiments.
